name: Juventus FC
content:
Juventus Football Club is one of the oldest and most successful football clubs in Italy, based in Turin. It was founded in 1897 by a group of students and initially played in pink shirts before adopting its iconic black-and-white striped kit in 1903. The club quickly rose to prominence, winning its first national championship in 1905 and becoming a dominant force in Italian football, especially during the 1930s when it secured multiple league titles.

Over the decades, Juventus has built a reputation as Italy’s most successful club, holding the record for the most league titles and numerous domestic trophies. The club has also achieved significant success in European and international competitions, including victories in the European Cup and UEFA Cup. Supported for many years by the Agnelli family, Juventus has attracted some of the world’s most famous players and maintained a strong presence at the highest level of football.

Despite its success, the club has also faced challenges and controversies. The most notable was the 2006 match-fixing scandal, which resulted in relegation to Serie B and the removal of league titles. Juventus quickly returned to the top division and reestablished itself as a dominant team, including a period of nine consecutive league titles in the 2010s. Today, it remains one of the most influential and widely supported football clubs in the world.

name: Inter Milan
content:
Inter Milan, officially known as Football Club Internazionale Milano, is one of the most historic and successful football clubs in Italy, based in Milan. It was founded in 1908 after a split from AC Milan, as a group of players wanted a club open to both Italian and foreign players, which inspired the name “Internazionale.” The club quickly achieved success, winning its first Italian championship in 1910.

Over its history, Inter has become one of Italy’s leading teams, winning numerous domestic trophies including multiple league titles, Coppa Italia trophies, and Supercoppa Italiana titles. The club enjoyed particularly strong periods, such as the late 2000s when it won five consecutive league titles. Inter has also been highly successful in international competitions, winning the European Cup or UEFA Champions League three times.

One of the most remarkable achievements in the club’s history came in 2010, when Inter became the first Italian team to win the treble, securing the league title, domestic cup, and Champions League in a single season. The club has never been relegated from Italy’s top division and plays its home matches at the San Siro stadium, which it shares with its city rival AC Milan. Today, Inter remains one of the most supported and influential football clubs in the world.

name: AC Milan
content:
AC Milan is one of the most historic and successful football clubs in Italy, based in Milan. Founded in 1899 as Milan Foot-Ball and Cricket Club, it has competed mainly in Serie A throughout its history. The club plays its home matches at San Siro, one of the largest stadiums in Italy, which it shares with its city rival Inter.

AC Milan has achieved major success both domestically and internationally. It is one of the most decorated clubs in world football, with numerous league titles and a record number of international trophies among Italian teams, including multiple European Cup and UEFA Champions League victories. The club is widely recognized for its iconic red-and-black colors and its long tradition of competing at the highest level.

The club has a famous rivalry with Inter Milan, with matches between the two known as the Derby della Madonnina, one of the most well-known derbies in football. Throughout its history, AC Milan has featured many legendary players and has built a large global fan base. Despite periods of difficulty, it remains one of the most influential and respected clubs in international football.

name: Genoa CFC
content:
Genoa Cricket and Football Club is the oldest football club in Italy, founded in 1893 in the city of Genoa. Originally established as a cricket and athletics club, it soon developed a football section that became dominant. The club played a key role in the early development of Italian football and was among the founders of the Italian Football Federation.

Genoa was the dominant force in the earliest Italian championships, winning the first official title in 1898 and securing several more in the following years. In total, the club has won nine Italian championships, most of them before the modern Serie A era. These early successes made Genoa one of the most important teams in the formative period of Italian football.

Although the club’s greatest achievements came in the early 20th century, Genoa has remained an important part of Italian football history. It has experienced periods of decline, including relegations and financial difficulties, but has also returned to the top division multiple times. Today, Genoa is respected for its historical legacy and its role as a pioneer of football in Italy.

name: Torino FC
content:
Torino Football Club is a historic Italian football club based in Turin, founded in 1906. It currently plays in Serie A and is known by the nicknames “Il Toro” and “I Granata,” reflecting its traditional maroon colors and the bull symbol of the city. The club was formed by a group of dissidents from Juventus along with members of earlier local teams, making it an important part of the early development of football in Turin.

Torino is one of Italy’s traditionally successful clubs, having won seven league titles and five Coppa Italia trophies. Its most famous period came in the 1940s with the legendary “Grande Torino” team, which dominated Italian football and won multiple championships in a row. This golden era ended tragically in 1949 when a plane crash in Superga killed almost the entire team, marking one of the most significant events in football history.

After the tragedy, the club experienced ups and downs but remained an important presence in Italian football. Torino won its most recent league title in 1976 and has continued to compete mainly in the top division. The club maintains a strong local identity and rivalry with Juventus, known as the Derby della Mole, and is respected for its history, passionate supporters, and contribution to Italian football.

name: Bologna FC
content:
Bologna FC is a historic Italian football club based in the city of Bologna, founded on 3 October 1909. It was created by a group of local and foreign enthusiasts, including Emilio Arnstein and Louis Rauch, who helped organize the first structured football activities in the city. The club’s traditional red-and-blue colors quickly became its identity, and it grew into one of the early pioneers of Italian football.

In its early decades, Bologna became one of the strongest teams in Italy, winning multiple national championships, especially during the 1920s and 1930s. The club claimed several league titles in that era, establishing itself as a major force in Italian football history. After World War II, Bologna continued to compete at a high level and won its last Serie A title in 1964, marking the end of its golden period.

Although its dominance declined in later years, Bologna remained an important and respected club in Italian football. It experienced periods of relegation and rebuilding but also achieved success in domestic cup competitions. Today, Bologna is known for its strong traditions, loyal fan base, and long-standing role in shaping the history of Italian football.

name: FC Pro Vercelli
content:
FC Pro Vercelli is an Italian football club based in Vercelli, Piedmont, and is considered one of the most important teams of the early era of Italian football. The club originated from a sports society founded in 1892, with its football section established in 1903. In its early decades, Pro Vercelli became a dominant force in national football and played a key role in shaping the development of the game in Italy.

Between 1908 and 1922, Pro Vercelli achieved its greatest success, winning seven national championships. During this period, the club was one of the strongest teams in the country and produced many players who also represented the Italian national team. However, with the rise of larger professional clubs in cities like Milan and Turin, Pro Vercelli gradually lost its dominance and entered a long period of decline.

After decades spent mostly outside the top division, the club went through financial difficulties and was effectively refounded in 2010, continuing the tradition of the historic team. Since then, Pro Vercelli has moved between the lower professional leagues of Italian football, occasionally reaching Serie B but without returning to its early glory. Today, it is recognized mainly for its historic legacy and its status as one of the pioneers of Italian football.

name: SSC Napoli
content:
SSC Napoli is a professional football club based in Naples, founded in 1926 after the merger of two local teams. The club plays its home matches at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona and is one of the most important teams in southern Italy. In its early years, Napoli had limited success but gradually established itself as a competitive side in Italian football.

The club’s first major success came in the 1960s with a Coppa Italia victory, followed by stronger performances in the 1970s and especially the 1980s. This golden era was defined by the arrival of Diego Maradona, who led Napoli to its first Serie A titles in 1987 and 1990, along with a UEFA Cup victory in 1989. These achievements marked the peak of the club’s early history and gave it international recognition.

After Maradona’s departure, Napoli faced financial problems and even bankruptcy in 2004, but the club was later rebuilt under new ownership and returned to Serie A. Since then, it has re-established itself among Italy’s top teams, winning multiple domestic trophies and again claiming league titles in recent years. Today, Napoli is recognized as one of the strongest and most popular clubs in Italian football.

name: AS Roma
content:
AS Roma is a professional football club based in Rome, Italy, founded in 1927 through the merger of several local teams. The club was created with the aim of giving the capital city a strong representative side capable of competing with the dominant northern clubs. It quickly became one of the main teams in Italian football and has played most of its history in the top division.

Roma has won the Italian league title three times and has also achieved success in domestic cup competitions, becoming one of the most supported clubs in the country. The team plays its home matches at the Stadio Olimpico, which it shares with its city rival Lazio. Matches between the two clubs form one of the most intense and famous rivalries in Italian football.

Throughout its history, Roma has featured many iconic players and strong squads, building a reputation for passionate football and a deep connection with its supporters. While it has often competed near the top of Italian football, the club is also known for periods of inconsistency. Despite this, AS Roma remains one of the most influential and recognizable teams in Italy and European football.

name: SS Lazio
content:
SS Lazio is a professional football club based in Rome, founded in 1900 as a sports society before developing its football section in the early 20th century. It is one of the oldest clubs in Italy and has traditionally played most of its history in the top division. The club is closely associated with its sky-blue and white colours and plays home matches at the Stadio Olimpico, which it shares with AS Roma.

In its sporting history, Lazio has achieved significant domestic and international success. The club has won multiple Italian league titles, Coppa Italia trophies, and Supercoppa Italiana titles. One of its most successful periods came in the late 1990s and early 2000s, when it also won European trophies such as the UEFA Cup Winners’ Cup and the UEFA Super Cup.

Lazio has also experienced ups and downs, including financial difficulties, relegation to Serie B, and scandals, but it has repeatedly returned to the top level of Italian football. Over time, it has built a strong rivalry with AS Roma known as the Derby della Capitale. Today, Lazio remains an established Serie A club with a long history and a solid position in Italian football.

name: ACF Fiorentina
content:
ACF Fiorentina is a professional football club based in Florence, Italy, founded in 1926 through the merger of two local teams. The club quickly established itself in Italian football and is known for its distinctive purple colours and the nickname “La Viola.” Fiorentina has traditionally played in Serie A for most of its history and is considered one of the most important clubs outside Italy’s biggest northern cities.

The club has achieved notable domestic and international success. Fiorentina has won two Serie A titles, several Coppa Italia trophies, and a Supercoppa Italiana. On the European stage, it became the first Italian team to win a UEFA-organised competition by claiming the Cup Winners’ Cup in 1961, and it has also reached multiple European finals over the years.

Fiorentina has experienced both success and serious difficulties, including financial collapse in 2002 that led to bankruptcy and re-founding. Despite this setback, the club quickly returned to the top levels of Italian football and re-established itself in Serie A. Today, Fiorentina remains a respected team with a strong fan base, a rich history, and regular competition in domestic and European tournaments.

name: Casale FBC
content:
Casale Foot Ball Club is one of the historic pioneers of Italian football, founded in 1909 in Casale Monferrato, Piedmont. The club quickly became part of the early competitive football scene in Italy and played a key role during the formative years of national competitions. Known for its black kit with a white star, Casale earned the nickname “Nerostellati.”

The club’s greatest achievement came in the 1913–14 season, when it won the Italian championship, becoming one of the early national champions of the country. During that era, Casale was able to compete with the strongest teams of the time and even achieved notable international recognition, including a famous victory over an English professional side in 1913.

After World War I, Casale gradually lost its top-level status as professional football in Italy developed and larger clubs became dominant. The team eventually dropped out of Serie A in the 1930s and spent most of its later history in lower divisions, with several financial restructurings and refoundations. Today, it is mainly remembered for its historic role and its early championship success in Italian football history.

name: USD Novese
content:
USD Novese is an Italian football club based in Novi Ligure, Piedmont, founded in 1919. The club was established by local sports enthusiasts and quickly became part of the early development of Italian football. It plays its home matches at the Stadio Costante Girardengo, a small stadium that has long been associated with the club’s history.

The most important moment in Novese’s history came in the 1921–22 season, when the club won the Italian Football Championship. This achievement is especially notable because it remains the club’s only national title and was earned during a period when Italian football was split into parallel competitions. Novese is often remembered as one of the surprise champions of early Italian football history.

After its early success, the club gradually declined as larger and more professional teams became dominant in Italy. Novese spent most of its later history in lower regional and amateur divisions, going through several reorganizations and periods of financial difficulty. Today, it is mainly recognized for its historic championship win and its unique place in the early history of Italian football.

name: Cagliari Calcio
content:
Cagliari Calcio is a professional football club based in Cagliari, Sardinia, founded in 1920. The club represents the island of Sardinia in Italian football and has traditionally been one of the most important teams from southern Italy and the islands. It plays its home matches in the city of Cagliari and is known for its red and blue colours.

The club’s greatest achievement came in the 1969–70 season, when it won its first and only Serie A title. That team, led by legendary striker Gigi Riva, became famous for its strong defensive record and dominance during the campaign. Cagliari also finished runner-up the previous season and established itself as a top side in Italian football during that era.

In European competitions, Cagliari has had more modest success, with its best run coming in the 1993–94 UEFA Cup when it reached the semi-finals. Over time, the club has moved between divisions but has remained an important symbol of Sardinian football. Today, it is recognized for its historic Scudetto victory and its strong regional identity.

name: Hellas Verona FC
content:
Hellas Verona Football Club is a professional Italian football team based in Verona, founded in 1903 by a group of students. The club takes its name from the Greek word “Hellas,” chosen by a classical studies professor, and it became the main representative team of the city after several early mergers with local sides. It has traditionally played its home matches at the Stadio Marcantonio Bentegodi.

For most of its history, Verona has moved between divisions, spending long periods outside the top flight before establishing itself more consistently in Serie A. The club’s golden era came in the 1980s, when it reached its highest competitive level and regularly competed near the top of the league. During this period, it also achieved strong runs in domestic cup competitions and participated in European tournaments, marking its peak as a competitive side.

The greatest achievement in Hellas Verona’s history came in the 1984–85 season, when the club won the Serie A title, a rare and historic triumph outside Italy’s traditional powerhouses. After this success, the team experienced a gradual decline but has continued to return to Serie A in different periods. Today, Verona is known as a resilient club with a strong identity and a reputation for occasional surprising performances against stronger opponents.

name: UC Sampdoria
content:
UC Sampdoria is a professional football club based in Genoa, Italy, founded in 1946 through the merger of Sampierdarenese and Andrea Doria. The new club adopted a unique identity combining elements from both predecessors, including its blue, white, red, and black colours. Sampdoria plays its home matches at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris, which it shares with Genoa CFC. The club quickly established itself in Serie A after its creation.

The club’s most successful period came in the late 1980s and early 1990s. During this era, Sampdoria won the Serie A title in 1991 and achieved major domestic success with multiple Coppa Italia victories. It also gained international recognition by winning the European Cup Winners’ Cup in 1990 and reaching the European Cup final in 1992. This golden generation featured legendary players such as Roberto Mancini and Gianluca Vialli.

After its peak, Sampdoria experienced fluctuations in performance, including relegations and promotions between divisions. In recent years, the club has faced financial and sporting difficulties, struggling to return to its former level of success. Despite this, Sampdoria remains an important Italian club with a strong fan base and a significant place in the history of Italian and European football.

name: SS Alba-Audace
content:
SS Alba-Audace was an Italian football club based in Rome, founded in 1907 in the Flaminio district. It originally started as Società Sportiva Alba and was one of the early football clubs in the city, playing an important role in the development of Roman football in the early 20th century. The club competed in the Italian Football Championship during its early years, when the competition structure was still regional and less organized.

In the mid-1920s, the club went through significant changes, including a forced merger with Audace Roma, which created the short-lived Alba-Audace identity. During this period, the team achieved strong results in southern Italian competitions, finishing among the top sides but falling short in national finals against northern clubs. Its competitive level made it one of the stronger Roman teams of its era before the major restructuring of football in the capital.

In 1927, Alba-Audace became one of the clubs merged to form AS Roma, alongside Roman FC and Fortitudo-Pro Roma, as part of an effort to create a strong representative team for the city. After the merger, the original club ceased to exist, though it was briefly reformed in later decades in lower divisions before finally disappearing. Today, it is remembered mainly for its role as one of the founding components of modern AS Roma and for its place in early Italian football history.

name: Internazionale FC Torino
content:
Internazionale Football Club Torino was an early Italian football club based in Turin, founded in 1891 through the merger of two older local sports clubs. These predecessor teams were among the first to introduce football to the city, influenced by English workers and early Italian sports enthusiasts. The new club adopted its identity and colours from one of the merging sides and became one of the pioneers of organized football in Italy.

The club played a key role in the very first Italian Football Championship in 1898, where it competed against other early teams such as Genoa and Ginnastica Torino. Internazionale Torino reached the final in both of the first two editions of the competition (1898 and 1899), finishing as runner-up on both occasions. During this period, it was considered one of the strongest teams in Italian football and helped establish the foundations of the national championship system.

In 1900, Internazionale Torino merged with Football Club Torinese, and the new entity continued under the Torinese identity. This marked the end of the club’s independent existence, but its legacy remained important in the early history of football in Turin. It is remembered today as one of the founding forces behind the development of Italian football and the structure of its first national competitions.

name: US Livorno
content:
US Livorno is an Italian football club based in Livorno, Tuscany, founded in 1915 after the merger of two local teams. The club quickly became part of the early Italian football system and is known for its traditional dark red colours and strong local identity. In its early decades, Livorno developed into one of the competitive sides in Italian football and took part in the highest national competitions.

Throughout its history, Livorno has experienced frequent movement between divisions, including several spells in Serie A, where it was even a founding member of the modern league system in 1929. The club’s best historical performances include finishing as runner-up in the national championship in 1919–20 and again in 1942–43. Over time, it became known as a classic “yo-yo club,” moving between top and lower divisions depending on the era.

In modern times, Livorno has faced financial difficulties, relegations, and even bankruptcy, which led to refoundings of the club. Despite these challenges, it has continued to return through the Italian football pyramid and maintain its identity. Today, it is recognized mainly for its historic role in Italian football and its passionate local support.

name: Parma Calcio
content:
Parma Calcio is an Italian football club based in Parma, Emilia-Romagna, founded in 1913. The club originated as Verdi Foot Ball Club and later became Parma Football Club, establishing itself in the early development of Italian football. It plays its home matches at the Stadio Ennio Tardini, which has been its historic stadium since the 1920s.

Throughout its history, Parma experienced long periods in the lower divisions before rising to prominence in the 1990s. This era became the most successful in the club’s history, during which it won multiple domestic and European trophies, including Coppa Italia titles and major UEFA competitions. The club also achieved its highest league performances during this golden period, becoming one of the strongest Italian teams of that decade.

In the 2000s, Parma faced severe financial problems linked to the collapse of its parent company, which eventually led to bankruptcy in 2015. The club was then refounded and restarted from the lower tiers of Italian football, achieving a rapid rise back to Serie A within a few seasons. Today, Parma is known for its resilience, strong identity, and its remarkable return to top-level football after complete rebuilding.

name: US Milanese
content:
US Milanese was an Italian football club based in Milan, founded in 1902. It was created by a group of local sports enthusiasts and quickly became one of the early teams involved in the development of organized football in Italy. The club was known for its distinctive black-and-white checkered kit, which earned it the nickname “Gli Scacchi” (the chessboard). It played an important role in Milan’s early football scene and competed in the Italian championships during the first decades of the 20th century.

During its competitive peak, US Milanese achieved strong results in the early national championships, including finishing as runner-up in the 1907–08 and 1908–09 seasons. It was considered one of the stronger teams in northern Italy at the time and was a regular competitor against other early football powers. However, as the sport became more professional and larger clubs emerged, its competitive level gradually declined.

In 1928, the club was forced to merge with Internazionale as part of a fascist-era restructuring of Italian football in Milan. This led to the creation of a new entity, ending US Milanese’s independent existence. Although it briefly reappeared in later years at a lower level, the club ultimately disappeared from professional football, leaving behind a legacy as one of the early pioneers of the game in Italy.

name: LR Vicenza
content:
LR Vicenza is a historic Italian football club based in Vicenza, founded in 1902, making it one of the oldest teams in the country. It is widely regarded as the main representative of football tradition in the Veneto region. Over time, the club has undergone several name changes and reorganizations, including periods as Lanerossi Vicenza and Vicenza Calcio, before its modern identity was established.

Throughout its history, Vicenza has spent many seasons in Italy’s top division, with its strongest era coming between the 1950s and 1970s when it was a regular Serie A side. The club’s most successful modern achievement came in 1996–97 when it won the Coppa Italia, marking its only major national trophy. It has also had notable European participation, reaching the semi-finals of the Cup Winners’ Cup in 1998.

In 2018, the club faced bankruptcy and was restructured, leading to the creation of the current LR Vicenza. Since then, it has competed mainly in the lower professional leagues while aiming to rebuild its status. Today, Vicenza is recognized for its long tradition, historical importance in Italian football, and its role as one of the oldest surviving clubs in northern Italy.

name: Fortitudo-Pro Roma
content:
Fortitudo-Pro Roma was an Italian football club based in Rome, formed in 1926 through the merger of Fortitudo and Pro Roma. Fortitudo itself had been founded in 1908 as a multi-sport society, and both clubs were active participants in the early Italian Football Championship. The merged team continued to compete in the Roman football scene during a period when the structure of Italian football was still regional and evolving.

The club played in the upper tiers of the southern Italian competitions and was considered one of the stronger Roman sides of its time. It had notable performances in the early 1920s, including deep runs in the national structure of the championship system before the creation of a unified Serie A. However, it was never able to win a national title, often falling short against stronger northern clubs.

In 1927, Fortitudo-Pro Roma SGS was dissolved as part of a major restructuring of football in the Italian capital. It was merged with Roman FC and Alba-Audace to form AS Roma, a new club intended to represent the city at a higher competitive level. After this merger, Fortitudo-Pro Roma ceased to exist as an independent team but remained an important part of Roma’s foundation history.

name: AC Perugia Calcio
content:
AC Perugia Calcio is an Italian football club based in the city of Perugia in the Umbria region, founded in 1905. The club was created through the merger of local sports societies and quickly became the main football representative of the area. Its traditional colours are red and white, and it plays home matches at the Stadio Renato Curi, named after a former player who died tragically during a match in 1977.

Throughout its history, Perugia has spent most of its time moving between divisions, but it has had several important periods of success. The club’s most famous era came in the 1970s, when it earned promotion to Serie A for the first time and later achieved a remarkable unbeaten league season in 1978–79, finishing second in the table. It has also had notable cup and European appearances in later decades, along with spells of decline caused by sporting and financial difficulties.

In more recent history, Perugia has faced multiple bankruptcies and refoundings, but it has continued to return to professional football. The club has moved between Serie B and lower divisions in the 21st century, rebuilding its structure each time under new ownership. Today, it is known as a traditional Italian club with a strong local identity and a history marked by both major achievements and repeated rebirths.

name: Pisa SC
content:
Pisa Sporting Club is an Italian football team based in the city of Pisa, Tuscany, founded in 1909. The club has a long and often turbulent history, involving multiple refoundings due to financial problems, including bankruptcies in 1994 and 2009. Despite these setbacks, it has repeatedly returned to professional football and continues to represent its city at a national level.

Throughout its history, Pisa has moved between divisions, spending periods in Serie A, Serie B, and lower leagues. Its most notable era came in the 1980s, when the club established itself in the top division and achieved strong results under influential leadership, also gaining attention in European competitions. The team plays its home matches at the Arena Garibaldi–Stadio Romeo Anconetani, a historic stadium closely tied to its identity.

In recent years, Pisa has rebuilt itself again after financial collapse, returning to higher professional levels and continuing its ambition to stabilize in top-tier football. The club is known for its passionate supporters and resilience, often symbolizing perseverance through repeated setbacks and recoveries. Today, it remains an established name in Italian football with a strong regional identity.

name: AC Sampierdarenese
content:
Associazione Calcio Sampierdarenese was an Italian football club based in the Sampierdarena district of Genoa, founded in 1899 as part of a local sports society. It was one of the early pioneers of football in Italy and played an important role in the development of the sport in the Liguria region. The club originally competed in the earliest regional and national championships during the first decades of Italian football.

Throughout its history, Sampierdarenese experienced several reorganizations, mergers, and name changes. In different periods it also competed under the name Liguria due to forced administrative changes, and it achieved some notable sporting success, including strong performances in second-tier competitions and participation in top-level Italian leagues. The club was competitive during the 1930s and 1940s, even returning to Serie A and producing respectable results despite instability.

In 1946, Sampierdarenese ceased to exist as an independent club when it merged with Andrea Doria to form UC Sampdoria, which became the main football representative of Genoa. This merger marked the end of its standalone history, but its identity, colours, and legacy were partially carried into the new club. Today, Sampierdarenese is remembered as one of the historic foundations of modern Genoese football and an important part of early Italian football development.

name: SSD Savoia FC
content:
SSD Savoia FC is an Italian football club based in Torre Annunziata, near Naples, founded in 1908. It is one of the oldest clubs in southern Italy and was originally created by local entrepreneurs linked to the flour and pasta industry. The team’s traditional white colours symbolise the city’s industrial heritage, and it has long played its home matches at the Stadio Alfredo Giraud.

In its early history, Savoia experienced its strongest period in the 1920s, when it competed at the highest level of Italian football and even reached the final of the national championship in 1923–24, finishing as runner-up. During that era, the club was one of the leading teams in southern Italy and regularly competed for regional and national honours. However, after this peak, it gradually declined as football in Italy became more centralized and professionalized.

In the following decades, Savoia moved between divisions and faced repeated financial and organizational difficulties, including bankruptcies and multiple refoundings. Despite these setbacks, the club has continued to return to competition in lower professional and semi-professional leagues, maintaining its identity and local support. Today, it is remembered mainly for its early success and its historic role in Italian football, particularly its remarkable run in the 1920s.

name: FBC Torinese
content:
FBC Torinese was an Italian football club based in Turin, founded in 1894. It was one of the earliest football teams in Italy and took part in the very first seasons of the Italian Football Championship. The club played a key role in the development of football in Turin during the sport’s formative years, competing against other pioneer teams from the region.

During its active years, Torinese was among the stronger early clubs in Italian football. It reached important stages of the national championship, including finishing as runners-up in 1900, and regularly competed in the early knockout-style tournaments. The team was also involved in several mergers and collaborations with other Turin-based clubs, reflecting the unstable and evolving structure of Italian football at the time.

In 1906, FBC Torinese ceased to exist as an independent club after merging with other local elements, including dissident members of Juventus, contributing to the creation of Torino FC. This marked the end of its standalone history but also its lasting legacy in forming one of Italy’s major football institutions. Today, it is remembered as one of the foundational clubs of early football in Turin and Italy as a whole.

name: US Triestina Calcio
content:
US Triestina Calcio is an Italian football club based in Trieste, founded in 1918 from the merger of two local teams, Ponziana and Foot-Ball Club Trieste. The club quickly became the main representative of football in the city and developed a strong identity tied to the Adriatic region. Its traditional nickname reflects its local roots and long-standing presence in Italian football.

Triestina reached a historic level in the early professional era, becoming one of the founding members of Serie A in 1929. The club remained in the top division for many years and achieved its greatest success in the 1947–48 season, finishing second in the league, which is still its best-ever result. During this period, it was considered a strong and competitive side in Italian football, often fighting against the dominant northern clubs.

After the 1950s, Triestina gradually lost its top-flight status and spent most of its history moving between Serie B and lower divisions. The club also experienced financial instability, reorganizations, and multiple refoundings, which affected its continuity. Despite these difficulties, it has remained an important symbol of football in Trieste and continues to compete in the Italian league system today, maintaining its historic identity and loyal local support.

name: Udinese Calcio
content:
Udinese Calcio is a professional football club based in Udine, in the Friuli-Venezia Giulia region of Italy. Founded in 1896, it is one of the oldest active football clubs in the country. The club is traditionally associated with black and white colours and is known by nicknames such as the “Zebrette,” reflecting its striped kit.

Throughout its history, Udinese has mostly competed between Serie A and Serie B, without ever winning the Italian league title. Its best domestic achievement came in the 1954–55 season, when it finished second in Serie A, marking its highest league finish. The club has also had several strong periods in top-flight football, including consistent participation in Serie A since the mid-1990s, with occasional qualification for European competitions.

On the international stage, Udinese has won a few minor European trophies, including the Intertoto Cup in 2000, as well as earlier victories in competitions like the Mitropa Cup and Anglo-Italian Cup. Despite financial limitations compared to larger Italian clubs, it is well known for developing and selling talented players. Today, Udinese is respected as a stable Serie A club with a strong scouting tradition and a reputation for discovering emerging talent.

name: Venezia FC
content:
Venezia FC is a professional football club based in Venice, founded in 1907 through the merger of two local sporting groups. It was created by around twenty football enthusiasts and quickly became the main representative of the city in early Italian competitions. In its early years, the club played its matches on the island of Sant’Elena and later established itself in national tournaments, taking part in the early stages of Italian football history.

Throughout its history, Venezia has mostly alternated between the top two divisions of Italian football. One of its greatest achievements came in 1941, when the club won the Coppa Italia, marking its most important domestic trophy. Over time, it experienced promotions and relegations, with several periods of rebuilding and fluctuating success in Serie A and Serie B.

In modern times, the club has undergone multiple reorganizations and refoundings due to financial instability, but it has repeatedly returned to professional football. Venezia is also known for its distinctive identity, stadium located on the lagoon island of Sant’Elena, and strong cultural connection to the city of Venice. Today, it remains a symbol of resilience and local pride in Italian football.

name: US Alessandria Calcio
content:
US Alessandria Calcio is a historic Italian football club based in Alessandria, Piedmont, founded in 1912. It is one of the oldest clubs in the country and became an important part of early Italian football development. The team is known by its nickname “I Grigi” due to its traditional grey kit and has long represented its city in national competitions.

The club experienced its strongest period in the early decades of Italian football, especially between the two World Wars, when it was part of the group of strong Piedmont teams that shaped the national game. Alessandria spent multiple seasons in Serie A and Serie B and reached the Coppa Italia final in 1936. Its greatest Serie A performances included high finishes in the early professional era of the league.

In later decades, Alessandria moved frequently between divisions and faced financial instability, including bankruptcy and refoundations. Despite these challenges, it continued to compete in Italian professional football and achieved occasional promotions, maintaining its historic identity. Today, it is recognized as a traditional club with deep roots in the origins of Italian football and a long-standing regional legacy.

name: Atalanta BC
content:
Atalanta Bergamasca Calcio is a professional football club based in Bergamo, Italy, founded in 1907 by students of the Liceo Classico Paolo Sarpi. The club takes its name from Atalanta, a figure in Greek mythology, and was formed after early football activity in the city developed through mergers with other local sports societies. It became officially established as Atalanta Bergamasca Calcio after a 1920 merger and has since become the main football team of Bergamo.

For much of its history, Atalanta moved between Serie A and Serie B, establishing itself as a strong “provincial” club in Italian football. It has spent many seasons in the top division but has traditionally been outside the group of Italy’s dominant clubs. Despite this, it has built a reputation for stability, consistent top-flight presence in modern decades, and one of the most respected youth academies in the country.

The club’s major achievements include winning the Coppa Italia in 1963 and, more recently, the UEFA Europa League in 2024, marking its first major European trophy. Atalanta has also regularly qualified for European competitions in the 21st century and reached the Champions League quarter-finals in 2020, reflecting its modern rise to higher competitive levels. Today, it is recognized as one of Italy’s most dynamic clubs, known for attacking football and strong player development.

name: FC Vado
content:
FC Vado is an Italian football club based in Vado Ligure, in the Liguria region, founded in 1913. It is one of the historic clubs of early Italian football and traditionally plays in red and blue colours. The team currently competes in the lower tiers of the Italian league system and plays its home matches at the Stadio Ferruccio Chittolina.

The club is best known for a unique achievement in Italian football history: it won the first-ever Coppa Italia in 1922. In the final, Vado defeated Udinese 1–0, securing the only major trophy in its history. This victory remains a remarkable milestone, as the club is still recognized as the inaugural winner of Italy’s main domestic cup competition.

After its early success, Vado spent most of its history outside the top divisions, moving between regional and lower national leagues. It faced periods of financial difficulty, interruptions during World War II, and later reorganization, but continued to exist and compete. Today, the club is mainly remembered for its historic cup triumph and its role in the early development of Italian football.

name: Palermo FC
content:
Palermo Football Club is a professional football team based in Palermo, Sicily, founded in 1900, making it one of the oldest clubs in Italy. Originally established as the Anglo Palermitan Athletic and Football Club, it became the main football representative of the island and is widely known by its nickname “Rosanero,” referring to its pink and black colours. The club currently competes in Serie B and is part of the City Football Group.

Throughout its history, Palermo has moved between different divisions, including 29 seasons in Serie A. Although it has not won the top division, it has achieved success in lower leagues, winning multiple Serie B titles and the Coppa Italia Serie C. The club has also reached the Coppa Italia final three times and participated in European competitions, especially during the 2000s when it gained wider international recognition.

Palermo’s history has been marked by several financial crises and refoundations, most recently in 2019, when the club was re-established and began again from the lower divisions. Despite these challenges, it quickly climbed back to professional football and remains the most prominent club from Sicily. Today, Palermo is known for its passionate fan base, strong regional identity, and ongoing efforts to return to the top level of Italian football.

name: Novara FC
content:
Novara Football Club is an Italian football team based in Novara, in the Piedmont region. The club was originally founded in 1908 by a group of students and became one of the early participants in organized Italian football. After financial problems led to the collapse of the historic Novara Calcio, a new entity was established in 2021 to continue the club’s tradition.

Throughout its history, Novara has spent most of its time between the second and third tiers of Italian football, although it has also played in Serie A for a total of 13 seasons. Its most successful period came between the late 1930s and 1950s, when the club regularly competed in the top division and achieved its best league finish of eighth place. Legendary striker Silvio Piola played for the team during this era and became closely associated with the club.

In more recent decades, Novara has experienced fluctuations between divisions along with financial instability, including losing its professional status in 2021. The club was quickly re-founded and returned to competition, winning promotion from Serie D back to Serie C. Today, Novara continues to compete in the lower professional leagues while maintaining its historical identity and legacy in Italian football.

name: Ars et Labor Ferrara Calcio
content:
Ars et Labor Ferrara Calcio, historically known as SPAL, is an Italian football club based in Ferrara, in the Emilia-Romagna region. It was founded in 1907 as a cultural and religious association before developing into a multi-sport club and later a professional football team. The club has long been the main football representative of the city and has played its home matches at the Stadio Paolo Mazza since 1928.

In its early years, the team gradually entered organized football competitions and reached Italy’s top division in the 1920s. Its most successful period came between the 1950s and 1960s, when it spent many seasons in Serie A and achieved its best-ever league finish of fifth place in the 1959–60 season. During this era, the club was known for developing talented players and maintaining a stable presence in the top flight.

In later decades, the club experienced fluctuations between divisions and several financial crises, leading to multiple bankruptcies and refoundations. After its most recent collapse, a new entity continuing its tradition was established in 2025 and began competing in lower regional leagues. Today, Ars et Labor Ferrara is recognized for its historical legacy in Italian football and its resilience through repeated rebirths.

name: US Catanzaro
content:
US Catanzaro 1929 is a professional Italian football club based in Catanzaro, in the Calabria region, founded in 1929. The team represents one of the main football institutions in southern Italy and plays its home matches at the Stadio Nicola Ceravolo. The club is traditionally known for its yellow and red colours and the nickname “Aquile del Sud,” reflecting its regional identity.

Throughout its history, Catanzaro has spent most of its time in the lower and middle tiers of Italian football, but it has also reached the top division. The club has played seven seasons in Serie A, with its best result being a seventh-place finish in the 1981–82 season. It also achieved notable success in cup competitions, reaching the Coppa Italia final in 1966 and winning several titles in lower divisions.

The club has experienced financial difficulties and was refounded multiple times, including major reorganizations in 2006 and 2011. Despite these challenges, Catanzaro has maintained its presence in Italian football and returned to higher divisions in recent years. Today, it competes in the professional league system and is recognized for its resilience, strong local support, and historic role in southern Italian football.

name: Calcio Padova
content:
Calcio Padova is an Italian football club based in Padua, in the Veneto region, founded in 1910. The team is known for its white and red colours and has long represented the city in national competitions. Over its history, the club has undergone several reorganizations, including a major refoundation in 2014 after financial collapse, before restoring its traditional name.

The club enjoyed its most successful period in the 1950s, when it became a strong force in Italian football. Under coach Nereo Rocco, Padova achieved its best-ever Serie A finish, placing third in the 1957–58 season. During this era, the team was known for its competitive performances in the top division and remained a regular participant in Serie A until the early 1960s.

After its peak, Padova experienced decades of fluctuation between divisions, including returns to Serie A such as in the 1990s, but also periods of decline into lower leagues. Financial difficulties led to bankruptcy in 2014, followed by a rapid rebuilding and return to professional football. Today, the club competes in the Italian league system and is recognized for its long tradition and resilience despite repeated setbacks.

name: AC Ancona
content:
AC Ancona was an Italian football club based in the city of Ancona, in the Marche region. Its origins date back to 1905 under the name Unione Sportiva Anconitana, and over time the club went through several name changes and reorganizations. The version known as Associazione Calcio Ancona was officially founded in 2004 as a successor to the original club. It played its home matches at the Stadio del Conero and was known by nicknames such as “I Dorici” and “I Biancorossi.”

Throughout its history, Ancona spent much of its time in the lower divisions but had notable moments in higher leagues. The club reached Serie A twice, with its most recent appearance in the 2003–04 season, although it struggled and finished with one of the lowest point totals in league history. It also reached the Coppa Italia final in the early 1990s, marking one of its most significant achievements at national level.

Financial instability played a major role in the club’s history, leading to repeated bankruptcies and refoundations. In 2010, AC Ancona was officially dissolved after going bankrupt, and several successor clubs were later created to continue football in the city. Today, the original club is remembered for its fluctuating history, brief appearances in top-flight football, and its role as a representative of the Marche region in Italian football.

name: Modena FC
content:
Modena Football Club 2018 is an Italian football club based in Modena, in the Emilia-Romagna region. The club traces its origins back to 1912, but the current entity was officially refounded in 2018 after the bankruptcy of the historic Modena FC in 2017. It continues the sporting tradition of the original team and plays its home matches at the Stadio Alberto Braglia.

Throughout its history, Modena has spent most of its time in Serie B, with several appearances in Serie A, totaling more than a decade in the top division. The club’s best performance in the top flight came in the 1946–47 season, when it finished in third place. It has also achieved success in lower divisions, winning Serie B twice and multiple titles in Serie C.

After its refoundation, Modena started again from the lower leagues and quickly progressed through the Italian football system. A key moment came in the 2021–22 season, when it won its Serie C group and earned promotion back to Serie B. Today, the club is considered a stable second-division team, known for its long tradition, resilience after financial collapse, and continued role in Italian football.
